title: Oman workers' federation January labor-violation reports
notes: The 17 January Oman Observer report discusses notifications and resolutions of individual workplace labor-violation cases; it does not describe a protest, strike or public gathering. Publication date only; no event date is inferred.

title: Omani Ministry of Labour employment assurance for 1,315 workers
notes: The article relays a government employment committee decision for 1,315 workers at 10 establishments; it reports neither a public gathering nor a strike/protest. Publication date only; worker headcount is not protest attendance.

title: Ministry of Labour job-nationalization decisions reported 24 January
notes: The report covers two ministry decisions reserving jobs for Omani nationals; it does not report a meeting, strike or protest. Publication date only; no event is inferred.

title: Oman Ministry of Labour negotiations over private-sector layoffs
notes: The report describes ministry/employer meetings over layoffs and recommendations to keep Omani employees in their jobs; no worker gathering, strike or public government demand is reported.

title: Calls to consider reopening Friday prayers after COVID restrictions
notes: The article vaguely reports that many people had called for Friday prayers to resume, but identifies no public meeting, march, sit-in, attendance, organizer or action date. It is not evidence of an event.

title: Omani Embassy safety alert concerning protest/gathering sites in Washington
notes: The Shabiba report relays a safety advisory to Omani citizens in Washington, D.C. about avoiding local gathering/protest sites and following the U.S. curfew. It does not report an action in Oman or a demand to Oman’s government.

title: Al Roya report of GFoW wage-deduction complaints and settlements, 17-28 January
notes: Opened Al Roya article (2021-01-31, body lines 99-113): it describes five GFoW complaints, settlement minutes and company referrals to prosecution during 17-28 January; it does not report workers gathering publicly, striking, marching or making a public collective demand. Complaint and settlement counts are not participants.

title: Oman Daily opinion on employment policy and possible accountability demands
notes: The full opinion discusses employment policy and says the public could demand accountability if government promises fail, conditionally and prospectively. It describes no actual public gathering, march, sit-in, strike, attendance or organizer; the conditional is not evidence of protest occurrence.

title: Oman Ministry committee employer meetings on retained workers
notes: Al Watan's full article describes a Ministry committee meeting with 12 companies and says 2,493 Omani employees were retained; it reports no worker protest, strike or public gathering. Article publication date is 12 January; an internal 'yesterday Tuesday' reference is inconsistent, so no precise meeting date is inferred. The workforce count is not attendance.

title: GFoW aggregate worker-complaint report spanning January-February
notes: The search extract reports 19 administrative worker complaints during 1 January-11 February and settlement/agreement records. It does not describe a public gathering or strike; the page remained inaccessible and full text was not opened. The date is the article's publication date, not an event date; the evidence does not establish that no action occurred.

title: GFoW worker-complaint report dated 31 January-4 February
notes: The opened Times of Oman article and Al Shabiba search extract describe five worker-rights reports, settlement records and federation work-team meetings during 31 January-4 February. They report no public gathering, protest or strike. The publication date is shown; this administrative complaint period is not an event date.
